key_insight: InSight makes vision-language-action (VLA) models steerable at the primitive-action level, letting them autonomously acquire new manipulation skills instead of being limited to what was seen in training. It turns demonstrations into a foundation for self-guided skill building through low-level action guidance like moving, lifting, and pouring.
problem_solved: VLA models can imitate demonstrated tasks, but they struggle to learn beyond the exact skills present in their training data. This paper addresses the challenge of enabling autonomous skill acquisition and more flexible manipulation without requiring exhaustive human demonstrations for every new behavior.
method: Automated segmentation pipeline breaks demonstrations into labeled primitive actions.
Primitive-level steering allows the VLA to follow fine-grained commands such as "move gripper to the bowl" or "lift upward."
A two-stage framework uses these primitives to support self-guided acquisition of more complex manipulation skills.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, InSight suggests a practical path toward more general, adaptive robot policies that can learn new skills with less manual supervision. This could reduce the cost of collecting task-specific data and improve robotic flexibility in real-world environments.
